mainTopic: The laws of תמורה: across kinds of animals, the extra words 'טוב', swapping with others' animals, and one-for-many versus one-for-one
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: a folk saying that a small thing in hand beats a bigger thing later. A new משנה then teaches that תמורה works across every kind of animal: flock and herd, sheep and goats, males and females, and blemished and unblemished. With blemished animals, it works only if the animal was made holy before it got its blemish. The גמרא finds the source in 'בהמה בבהמה'. אביי and רבא then argue over how the extra words 'טוב' in the פסוק teach the timing rule and the מלקות for swapping good for good. A ברייתא explains why the Torah uses two verbs for swapping, and the גמרא shows how a person can swap with someone else's holy animal: its owner gave permission. A second משנה brings a dispute: the תנא קמא allows one animal for many, while רבי שמעון allows only one for one. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן then argue whether רבי שמעון allows swapping the same holy animal a second time, and each has a ברייתא on his side. The amud ends as רבי אבין begins a question about an אשם that was swapped, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A zucchini now is better than a gourd later
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the previous discussion: a folk saying that something you have now is worth more than something bigger you might get later.
steps.simpleTranslation: A small zucchini in hand is better than a big gourd you might get later.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a discussion that started on the previous daf. The גמרא ends it with a well-known saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying makes a practical point: people prefer something certain now over something bigger but uncertain later. The גמרא uses it to show how a person would really think, which settles the earlier point. Right after it, a brand-new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A small squash or zucchini, something modest you already have
A large gourd, something bigger you only hope to get later
Good, better (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this קָרָא (gourd) with the more common word קְרָא (a פסוק). Here it means a vegetable.

phrases.english: A zucchini now is better than a gourd later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: People value something certain now over something bigger but uncertain later.

steps.title: The משנה: תמורה works across all kinds of animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that תמורה works between flock and herd, sheep and goats, males and females, and unblemished and blemished animals, in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can make a תמורה from flock animals onto herd animals and the other way around. Also from sheep onto goats and goats onto sheep, from males onto females and females onto males, and from unblemished animals onto blemished ones and blemished onto unblemished.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists pairs of different animal types and says תמורה works between each pair, in either direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה is when someone tries to swap a regular animal for a קרבן animal. The swap is forbidden, but the new animal still becomes holy. The משנה teaches that the two animals do not have to be the same kind: a cow can become holy as a תמורה for a sheep, and so on.

keyTerms.meaning: One makes a תְּמוּרָה, meaning you declare a regular animal as a replacement for a consecrated one
Flock animals: sheep and goats
Herd animals: cattle
Unblemished animals, fit for the מזבח
Blemished animals, unfit for the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מְמִירִין מִן הַצֹּאן עַל הַבָּקָר,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One makes a substitution from the flock onto the herd,
phrases.notes: The first animal is the consecrated one, and the second is the regular animal that becomes holy.

phrases.english: and from the herd onto the flock,
and from the sheep onto the goats,
and from the goats onto the sheep,
from the males onto the females,
and from the females onto the males,
from the unblemished onto the blemished,
from the blemished onto the unblemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמורה takes effect even when the two animals are of different kinds, sexes, or blemish status, in either direction.

steps.title: The משנה's source: 'good for bad or bad for good'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings the פסוק 'לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו טוב ברע או רע בטוב' as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He shall not exchange it or substitute it, good for bad or bad for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its rule, especially the blemished and unblemished pairs, with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about swapping 'good' for 'bad' and 'bad' for 'good'. That shows a תמורה can happen between a better animal and a worse one, meaning unblemished and blemished.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not exchange it
And he shall not substitute, the root of the word תְּמוּרָה
Good for bad: a better animal in exchange for a worse one

phrases.english: As it is stated: "He shall neither exchange it nor substitute it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: good for bad or bad for good";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the ruling in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That תמורה works between unblemished and blemished animals

steps.title: What case is 'good for bad'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what case the פסוק means by 'טוב ברע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the case of 'good for bad'?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה stops to define a phrase from the פסוק. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a puzzle here. A blemished animal usually cannot become a real קרבן, so how can it be the holy animal in a swap? The question asks when the פסוק's case can really happen.

keyTerms.meaning: And which is it, a request to define a case

phrases.english: And which is "good for bad"?
phrases.notes: Here the 'bad' one, the blemished animal, is the holy one, and the 'good' regular animal is swapped onto it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a phrase from the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case is a blemished animal holy, so that a good animal can be swapped onto it?

steps.title: Blemished animals that were consecrated before their blemish
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'טוב ברע' means blemished animals that were consecrated first and got their blemish afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blemished animals whose consecration came before their blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. The case is an animal that was made holy while healthy and only later got a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an animal was fully holy as a real קרבן before it got the blemish, so a swap onto it still works. If the animal was already blemished when it was consecrated, only its value is holy, and תמורה does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecration, making something holy
Came first, preceded
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: תמורה works across all types of animals. With blemished animals, it works only if the animal was consecrated before it got its blemish.

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן.
phrases.english: Blemished animals whose consecration preceded their blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'טוב ברע' refers to a blemished holy animal that was consecrated before it got its blemish.

steps.title: The גמרא asks: where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that תמורה works across different kinds of animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's list. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק the משנה quoted, 'טוב ברע', only covers good and bad, meaning unblemished and blemished. It does not show that flock works with herd, or males with females. So the גמרא wants a source for the whole list.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned? A request for a source
The discussion that explains the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא forgot that the משנה already quoted a פסוק. That פסוק only covers blemished and unblemished, so a source is still needed for the other pairs.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for תמורה working across different species, sexes and blemish status.

steps.title: The ברייתא: 'an animal for an animal' covers every pair
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'בהמה בבהמה' that תמורה works across every pair the משנה listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: 'An animal for an animal' teaches that you can make a תמורה from flock onto herd and herd onto flock, sheep onto goats and goats onto sheep, males onto females and females onto males, blemished onto unblemished and unblemished onto blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The source is the words 'בהמה בבהמה' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the general word 'בהמה', animal, for both sides of the swap. So any animal can be swapped for any other animal, and every pair in the משנה is included. The ברייתא lists the same pairs as the משנה, with only the last pair in reverse order.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal for an animal: the general wording that includes all kinds
From here, meaning this is the source
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The source for תמורה across all kinds of animals is the general phrase 'בהמה בבהמה' (ויקרא 27:10).
steps.whyThisMatters: The holiness of תמורה does not depend on the new animal matching the original. Any domestic animal can become holy through it.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "An animal for an animal":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10, the same פסוק as the משנה, from a later part of it.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן שֶׁמְּמִירִין מִן הַצֹּאן עַל הַבָּקָר,
phrases.english: from here we learn that one substitutes from the flock onto the herd,
and from the herd onto the flock,
from the sheep onto the goats,
and from the goats onto the sheep,
and from the males onto the females,
and from the females onto the males,
and from the blemished onto the unblemished,
and from the unblemished onto the blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The general phrase 'בהמה בבהמה' includes every kind of animal, so תמורה works across all the משנה's pairs.

steps.title: Maybe even animals blemished before being made holy?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the possibility that blemished animals can have a תמורה even if the blemish came before they were made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: even if the blemish came before they were made holy, a תמורה would work?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and suggests a possible mistake: maybe every blemished animal can have a תמורה, no matter when the blemish came. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said blemished animals can have a תמורה. Now it asks whether that includes an animal that was already blemished when it was made holy. The word יכול shows this is a thought the ברייתא is about to reject.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': a possible idea the ברייתא is about to reject
A blemish that makes an animal unfit to be brought as a קרבן
Making an animal holy for the בית המקדש

phrases.english: One might think: even if the blemish came before their consecration?
phrases.notes: He means: would a תמורה still work for such an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 7 by narrowing which blemished animals are included.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a תמורה work for an animal that was already blemished when it was made holy?

steps.title: Only if it was made holy before the blemish
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses the פסוק 'טוב ברע' to limit the rule to animals that were made holy first and became blemished later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall not exchange it nor substitute it, good for bad or bad for good.' Which case is 'good for bad'? Blemished animals that were made holy before they got their blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the פסוק: the 'bad' animal in the פסוק is one that was made holy while still unblemished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was holy and only later got a blemish keeps a stronger holiness, so a תמורה works for it. An animal that was blemished first and only then made holy does not. This is the same reading the משנה gave in step 5, now as part of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': brings a פסוק to settle the question
'Good for bad': swapping an unblemished animal for a blemished holy one
Blemished animals

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"He shall neither exchange it nor substitute it,
good for bad or bad for good,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: And which is "good for bad"?

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן.
phrases.english: Blemished animals whose consecration came before their blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 8 and rejects it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Only animals made holy before they got their blemish can have a תמורה.
steps.whatToRemember: A blemished animal can have a תמורה only if it was made holy first and got the blemish later.

steps.title: How does the פסוק show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא learns the timing rule from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the derivation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק show that the timing of the blemish matters. This sets up the answers of אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'which is good for bad?' and gave the answer, but did not show which word in the פסוק teaches it. The גמרא wants the exact source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the derivation?': which word teaches this

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual source behind the ruling in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words of the פסוק teach that a blemish before הקדש blocks תמורה?

steps.title: אביי: the extra word 'בטוב' teaches it
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the פסוק could have said 'רע בו' ('bad for it'). The extra word 'בטוב' teaches that only an animal that was good from the start can have a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the פסוק could have said 'He shall not exchange it nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for it.' Why do I need another 'for good'? Learn from it: an animal that was good from the start makes a תמורה; one that was bad from the start does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finds a word the פסוק did not need, 'בטוב', and uses it as the source for the timing rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'bad for it' would already point back to the holy animal, so writing 'good' again is extra. אביי reads the extra 'good' as a description of the holy animal: it must have been good, meaning unblemished, when it was first made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need it?': points to an extra word
'Learn from it': the lesson taken from the extra word
From its start, meaning when it was first made holy
Substitution: trying to swap a holy animal for another, which makes the new one holy too

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Let the verse say:
"He shall neither exchange it nor substitute it,
good for bad, or bad for it,"
phrases.notes: 'For it' would already point back to the holy animal, so the word 'good' would not be needed.

phrases.english: Why do I need another "for good"?
Learn from it:
an animal good from its start makes a substitute,
one bad from its start does not make a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'בטוב' teaches that only an animal that was good from the start makes a תמורה.

steps.title: רבא: both words 'טוב' are extra and teach two lessons
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both words 'טוב' could have been left out. One teaches that even swapping good for good earns מלקות; the other teaches the timing rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: both words 'good' are extra. If so, let the פסוק write 'He shall not exchange it nor substitute it for bad, or bad for it.' Why write 'good' twice? One 'good' teaches that even good for good, one who substitutes gets lashes. The other 'good' teaches that an animal good from the start makes a תמורה, and one bad from the start does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different reading. He says both words 'good' are extra, so the פסוק teaches two separate lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the פסוק could have mentioned only 'bad'. The first extra 'good' adds that swapping an unblemished animal for another unblemished one is also forbidden and earns מלקות. The second extra 'good' gives the same timing rule as אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are completely extra': both words are not needed for the plain meaning
He gets מלקות, lashes
One who substitutes, who tries to make a תמורה

phrases.english: Rava said:
Both instances of "good" are extra.
If so, let the verse write:
"He shall neither exchange it nor substitute it
for bad, or bad for it."
Why do I need it to write both instances of "good"?
One "good" teaches: even good for good too,
when he substitutes, he is flogged.
And the other "good" teaches: an animal good from its start makes a substitute,
one bad from its start does not make a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the פסוק from אביי's in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both words 'טוב' are extra: one teaches מלקות for good-for-good, the other teaches the timing rule.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא agree on both הלכות. They only disagree about whether the מלקות for good-for-good need their own word in the פסוק.

steps.title: Why אביי does not need a word for good-for-good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that אביי learns the lashes for good-for-good from a קל וחומר, so he needs only one extra word.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי says: it is a קל וחומר. If one who swaps good for bad, which improves the holy animal, gets lashes, then one who swaps good for good, where the two are equal, surely gets lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי does not read the פסוק like רבא. He does not need a word to teach lashes for good-for-good, because simple logic already proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swapping a blemished holy animal for an unblemished one actually improves things, and the פסוק still punishes it. Swapping one unblemished animal for an equal one has no benefit at all, so it is surely punished. Since logic covers this, אביי needs only one extra word, for the timing rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a weaker case to a stronger case
He is improving it, giving the holy side a better animal
All the more so

phrases.english: And Abaye says: it is an a fortiori inference,
just as good for bad,
where he is improving it, he is flogged,
phrases.notes: The holy animal was blemished, and he offers an unblemished one in its place, so the holy side gains.

phrases.english: good for good, which are equal to each other,
is it not all the more so that he is flogged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אביי's approach against רבא's by showing that רבא's first lesson does not need a word in the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבא's need for a separate word teaching lashes for good-for-good, not the halacha itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A word in the פסוק is not needed for something a קל וחומר already proves.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees: swapping good for good earns מלקות, and only an animal unblemished when made holy can have a תמורה. אביי learns the first by קל וחומר; רבא learns it from an extra 'טוב'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way the גמרא works: an extra word in a פסוק is not used for a law that logic can already prove.

steps.title: רבא: no punishment from a logical derivation
steps.stepSummary: רבא needs an extra word in the פסוק because we do not give lashes based on a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא holds: we do not punish based on a logical derivation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא does not accept אביי's קל וחומר for good-for-good lashes. A punishment needs a פסוק, not just logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13, אביי learned the good-for-good lashes from a קל וחומר. רבא answers with a general rule: אין עונשין מן הדין. Lashes must come from the words of the פסוק, so רבא needs one extra word 'טוב' for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not punish based on a logical derivation (a קל וחומר)
Lashes given as a punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known rule that comes up across ש״ס: a punishment must have its own source in a פסוק.

phrases.english: And Rava:
one does not punish based on a logical derivation.
phrases.notes: Here 'הדין' means the קל וחומר that אביי used in the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר אביי used in step 13, explaining why רבא still needs a separate extra 'טוב'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why doesn't רבא learn good-for-good lashes from a קל וחומר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lashes cannot be based on a קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's use of a קל וחומר as the source for lashes in the good-for-good case. רבא does not dispute that good-for-good is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Lashes cannot be based on a קל וחומר (אין עונשין מן הדין). They need an explicit word in the פסוק.

steps.title: אביי: good-for-good is obvious from the verse itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the good-for-good case is not a real קל וחומר. It is plainly included in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי can tell you: this is not a logical derivation. Is swapping a good animal any less of a swap than swapping a bad one?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself against רבא's rule. He says he is not punishing from logic at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי admits we do not punish from a קל וחומר. But he holds that if the פסוק forbids swapping in a bad animal, it obviously also forbids swapping in a good one. That is just the plain meaning of the prohibition, so the rule against punishing from logic does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it any worse or any less?
A good (unblemished) animal compared with a bad (blemished) one

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not disagree with the rule 'אין עונשין מן הדין'. He only says his case is not a real דין in the first place.

phrases.english: And Abaye can say to you:
this is not a logical derivation;
is good any less than bad?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבַּיֵּי אָמַר לָךְ: הָא לָאו דִּינָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אביי against רבא's objection in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasts the derivation as the plain meaning of the פסוק, not a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי seems to be punishing from a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Good-for-good is simply part of what the פסוק forbids.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי needs only one extra 'טוב' (for the timing rule). רבא needs both: one for good-for-good lashes, which cannot come from logic, and one for the timing rule.

steps.title: ברייתא: one phrase for others' animals, one for his own
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ' is about swapping for someone else's animal, and 'וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ' is about swapping for his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'He shall not exchange it' refers to another person's animal, and 'nor substitute it' refers to his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that explains the two words the Torah uses for swapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two different verbs for swapping. The ברייתא gives each verb its own job. One covers a swap involving another person's animal, and the other covers a swap involving one's own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not exchange it
Nor shall he substitute it
With an animal belonging to others

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"He shall not exchange it" refers to that of others,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: "nor substitute it" refers to his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the אביי/רבא discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two verbs in the פסוק cover two cases: another person's animal and one's own.

steps.title: Why not write only 'He shall not exchange it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah needs both verbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write only 'He shall not exchange it', and there would be no need for 'nor substitute it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If swapping involving others is forbidden, then swapping your own should be forbidden all the more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the second verb looks extra. If the Torah forbids even a swap that involves someone else's animal, it should be obvious that a swap of one's own animal is forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it write (only)
It would not be needed

phrases.english: But let it write "He shall not exchange it,"
and there is no need for "nor substitute it"!
phrases.notes: The idea is that one's own case would follow 'all the more' from the case of others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִכְתּוֹב ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ״, וְלָא בָּעֵי ״לֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the second verb 'וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One verb seems enough, since one's own case could be learned from the case of others.

steps.title: The second verb covers a swap that makes both animals holy
steps.stepSummary: Without the second verb, we might think lashes apply only to the wording 'this one leaves, this one enters', and not to plain תמורה, which makes both animals holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah wrote only that, I would think a person gets lashes only when he says 'let this one leave and this one enter'. But one who makes a תמורה, which makes both animals holy, would not get lashes. So the Torah teaches us that he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each verb is needed for a different kind of swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יחליפנו' sounds like a real trade, where the holy status leaves one animal and goes into the other. A regular תמורה does not take anything away: the first animal stays holy and the second animal also becomes holy. We might have thought that is not a 'swap' worth lashes, so 'ימיר' teaches that it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Let this one leave (holiness) and this one enter
One who makes a תמורה
It teaches us (otherwise)
I would have thought

phrases.english: If it had written that way,
I would have said:
"Let this one leave and this one enter":
it is that case in which he is flogged;
but one who effects substitution,
since he consecrates both of them,
I would say he is not flogged.
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verb covers a different kind of swap
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lashes apply only to a true trade of holiness ('leave and enter').
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain תמורה, which makes both animals holy, also brings lashes.

steps.title: What case is 'another person's animal'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of swapping with another person's animal looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case of 'that of others': what are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking what the ברייתא's case actually is. The next steps test the possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A swap involves two animals: a holy one and a non-holy one. Either one could belong to someone else. The גמרא is about to check each option.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?

phrases.english: This case of "that of others,"
what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of Step 16 to define its case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which animal belongs to the other person: the holy one or the non-holy one?

steps.title: He cannot make someone else's animal holy
steps.stepSummary: If the holy animal is his and the non-holy animal belongs to someone else, he cannot make that other animal holy, because one can only consecrate what he owns.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the holy animal is his and the non-holy one belongs to someone else, can he make it holy? The Torah says 'When a man shall consecrate his house': just as his house is his, so too anything he consecrates must be his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה makes the non-holy animal holy. If that animal belongs to someone else, this person has no power to make it holy. The פסוק about 'ביתו' teaches that a person can only consecrate what is his.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-holy, ordinary property
Belonging to anyone else (literally: of the world)
In his possession or ownership
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: If we say
the consecrated animal is his,
and the non-sacred one belongs to others,
is he able to consecrate it?

phrases.aramaic: ״אִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּישׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״
phrases.english: "When a man shall consecrate his house to be holy to the Lord"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:14

phrases.english: the Merciful One said;
just as his house is in his possession,
so too anything must be in his possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא בְּהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ דִּידֵיהּ, וְחוּלִּין דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible case raised by Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the non-holy animal belongs to someone else
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot consecrate property he does not own (from 'ביתו').

steps.title: He cannot make a תמורה on someone else's holy animal
steps.stepSummary: If the holy animal belongs to someone else and the non-holy one is his, how can he make a תמורה on something that is not his?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say the holy animal belongs to someone else and the non-holy one is his. Can a person make a תמורה on something that is not his?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option and finds a problem with it as well. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the new animal is his, so he can make it holy. But a תמורה works by connecting it to the holy animal, and that holy animal belongs to someone else. The גמרא doubts that a person can attach holiness through an item that is not his.

keyTerms.meaning: Attaches holiness to an item by linking it to an already-holy item
Something that does not belong to him

phrases.english: But rather, the consecrated animal belongs to others,
and the non-sacred one is his:
can one effect substitution with an item that is not his?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ דְּעָלְמָא, וְחוּלִּין דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible case after the first was rejected in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the holy animal belongs to someone else
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot make a תמורה by linking to a holy item he does not own.

steps.title: The owner gave everyone permission to swap
steps.stepSummary: The case is a holy animal belonging to someone else, where its owner told everyone they may make a תמורה with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, we are talking about a holy animal that belongs to someone else and a plain animal that belongs to him. For example, the owner of the holy animal said: 'Anyone who wants to make a swap with my animal may come and do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21: how can a person make a תמורה on a holy animal that is not his? The answer is that the owner gave public permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said a person cannot make a תמורה on an animal he does not own. The answer keeps the case of someone else's הקדש but adds that the owner allowed others to swap. With that permission, the other person's swap counts, and his own חולין animal becomes holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to hold on to an earlier idea and explain it better
A holy animal that belongs to someone else
Plain, non-holy property
To make a תמורה (swap a plain animal for a holy one)

steps.whatToRemember: A person can make a תמורה on someone else's holy animal if its owner gave permission.

phrases.english: Actually, it is about a holy animal that belongs to others,
and the plain animal is his own,
for example, where the owner of the holy animal said:
"Whoever wants to make a swap with his animal, let him come and swap."
phrases.notes: "His animal" here means the owner's holy animal. He is opening it up for anyone to swap with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a condition to the case: the owner gave permission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person can never make a תמורה on a holy animal he does not own.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the owner said anyone may swap, another person's תמורה works.

steps.title: The משנה: one animal may be swapped for many, and many for one
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא of the new משנה rules that a תמורה can be made one for two, two for one, one for a hundred, and a hundred for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may swap one animal for two, and two for one, one for a hundred, and a hundred for one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a תמורה does not have to be one animal for one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may swap one plain animal for several holy animals, or several plain animals for one holy animal. The number on each side does not have to match. All the plain animals become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; the start of a new משנה
One makes a תמורה / one swaps

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may swap one animal for two,
phrases.notes: One plain animal for two holy ones; the next line is the reverse.

phrases.english: and two for one,
one for a hundred, and a hundred for one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה works even when the numbers do not match: one for many or many for one.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only one animal for one animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and allows only one for one, learning from the word 'הוא' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: One may swap only one for one, as it says: 'It and its substitute shall be holy.' Just as 'it' is one single animal, so too its substitute must be one single animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues on the first opinion and limits תמורה to one animal for one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the holy animal 'הוא' (it), which is one animal. רבי שמעון reads the substitute the same way: just as the holy animal is one, the substitute must also be one. So the numbers must match, one for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Single, one specific item
Its substitute (the animal swapped for it)
Just as ... so too; a way of comparing two things

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
One may swap only one for one,
as it says: "It and its substitute shall be holy,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: just as "it" is one single animal,
so too its substitute is one single animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְמִירִין אֶלָּא אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה works only one animal for one animal.

steps.title: Where does this come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rules. It is setting up the next move, where it will bring a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון gave a source in the משנה, but the תנא קמא did not. The גמרא wants to see where each side's view comes from in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these things learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the rules of the משנה

steps.title: The ברייתא: 'בהמה בבהמה' allows any numbers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'בהמה בבהמה' that one may swap one for many and many for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'An animal for an animal.' From here we learn that one may swap one for two, two for one, one for a hundred, and a hundred for one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The תנא קמא learns his view from the words 'בהמה בבהמה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא reads 'בהמה' as a general word for animals, so it can mean one or many. That is why the numbers on each side do not need to match.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal for an animal (the פסוק about תמורה)
From here (we learn)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"An animal for an animal"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: from here we learn that one may swap one for two,
and two for one,
one for a hundred, and a hundred for one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא learns from 'בהמה בבהמה' that the numbers on each side may differ.

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads the same words as singular
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון learns from the same words that only one for one is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: One may swap only one for one, as it says 'an animal for an animal', and not 'an animal for animals', and not 'animals for an animal'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's view. He uses the very same words to prove the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון focuses on the fact that 'בהמה' is singular on both sides. If the Torah meant to allow many, it would have said 'בהמות'. Here the ברייתא itself repeats his ruling, now with a new proof that differs from the one in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals (plural)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְמִירִין אֶלָּא אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: One may swap only one for one,
as it says "an animal for an animal,"
and not "an animal for animals,"
and not "animals for an animal."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְמִירִין אֶלָּא אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one for one, because 'בהמה' is singular.

steps.title: A group of animals can be called 'בהמה'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא challenges רבי שמעון from יונה, where many animals are called 'בהמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We have found that many animals are called 'בהמה', as it says: 'and many animals' (וּבְהֵמָה רַבָּה).
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא קמא pushes back against רבי שמעון's proof from the singular word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that 'בהמה' means only one animal. The תנא קמא shows a פסוק where the singular word 'בהמה' describes a large group. So the singular form does not prove that only one animal is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: And many animals (יונה 4:11)
We have found (a proof from elsewhere)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא answering רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: We have found many animals that are called "בהמה",
as it says: "and many animals."
phrases.notes: יונה 4:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מָצִינוּ בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁקְּרוּיָה בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's reading in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that singular 'בהמה' means only one animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק uses singular 'בהמה' for a large group, so the singular form proves nothing.

steps.title: Only 'בהמה רבה' means many, not plain 'בהמה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that a group is called 'בהמה רבה', but never plain 'בהמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון would say: a group is called 'בהמה רבה' (many animals), but it is not called plain 'בהמה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's answer to the challenge, so his view still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יונה the word 'רבה' (many) is added, and that is what makes it a group. Plain 'בהמה' with nothing added still means one animal. So the פסוק of תמורה, which says just 'בהמה', means one for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain, with nothing added
Is called

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא allows a תמורה of one for many or many for one. רבי שמעון allows only one for one, because plain 'בהמה' means one animal.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon would say:
they are called "many animals,"
but they are not called plain "בהמה."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 for רבי שמעון
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tells the two פסוקים apart: the word 'רבה' makes the difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'בהמה' can mean a group, the תמורה פסוק may allow many animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'בהמה רבה' means a group. Plain 'בהמה' means one animal.

steps.title: Which word is really רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the משנה said רבי שמעון learns from the word 'הוא', not from 'בהמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי שמעון's reason really the word 'בהמה'? The משנה said his reason is the word 'הוא': just as 'it' means one specific animal, the substitute must also be one specific animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two sources give different reasons for רבי שמעון. The ברייתא says 'בהמה', but the משנה says 'הוא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 had רבי שמעון learning one-for-one from 'בהמה בבהמה'. The משנה gave a different source: 'הוא' is singular, so the תמורה must also be a single animal. Both cannot be his real source, so the גמרא asks which one it is.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a contradiction)
'It': a singular word in the פסוק, used to show one specific animal
Specific, single, set apart
The substitute animal that a person tries to swap for a holy animal

phrases.english: And the reason of Rabbi Shimon
is it because of the word "animal"?
But isn't the reason of Rabbi Shimon
because of the word "it",
just as "it" means one specific animal,
so too the substitute must be one specific animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִשּׁוּם ״בְּהֵמָה״ הוּא? וְהָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִשּׁוּם ״הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source the ברייתא gave for רבי שמעון in steps 27 to 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that רבי שמעון learns one-for-one from 'בהמה בבהמה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says רבי שמעון learns it from 'הוא'. The two sources seem to contradict each other about his reason.

steps.title: רבי שמעון used both sources, one after the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון first used 'הוא'. After the Rabbis used 'בהמה בבהמה', he showed that their פסוק also supports him.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first רבי שמעון argued from 'והיה הוא ותמורתו'. When he saw the Rabbis learning from 'בהמה בבהמה', he told them: I can learn my view from that phrase too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction, because רבי שמעון gave both sources. 'הוא' was his first source, and 'בהמה' was his reply to the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הוא' is רבי שמעון's main source, which is why the משנה quotes it. In the ברייתא he answers the Rabbis using their own פסוק and shows it can be read his way. So both reports are true.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, originally
They expound, they learn out from a פסוק
From there too
To learn out, to derive

phrases.english: At first Rabbi Shimon told them
from "then both it and its substitute,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: and when he saw that the Rabbis learned
from "an animal for an animal,"
he said to them:
from there too we are able
to learn the reason for my view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sources are correct; they were said at different stages of the debate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the משנה and the ברייתא disagree about רבי שמעון's source.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הוא' is his main source. 'בהמה בבהמה' was a later reply that turned the Rabbis' own פסוק to his side.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's main source for one-for-one is 'הוא'. He used 'בהמה בבהמה' only to answer the Rabbis with their own פסוק.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי שמעון allows swapping the same animal again
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רבי שמעון agrees that one may make a תמורה and then make another תמורה with the same holy animal, because its holiness never left.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון agrees that a person may swap, and then swap again. Why? Where did the original holiness of the הקדש animal go?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. ריש לקיש says that even רבי שמעון allows a second swap with the same holy animal, one swap after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the first swap, the original animal stays fully holy. Its holiness was not used up, so it can make a second animal holy as well. רבי שמעון only forbids swapping many animals at one time.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
One makes a תמורה, and then makes another תמורה again
The original holiness
Something made holy, given to the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: 'Swap and swap again' is not the same as swapping two at once. Here the same holy animal is swapped once, and later swapped again for another animal.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
that one may swap, and then swap again,
what is the reason?
The original holiness of the consecrated animal,
where did it go?!
phrases.notes: He means it went nowhere. The animal is still just as holy as before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁמְּמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about how far רבי שמעון's one-for-one rule goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון allows a second, separate תמורה with the same holy animal, because its holiness stays.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: no second swap either
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that just as רבי שמעון forbids swapping two for one, he also forbids swapping again with the same animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: just as one cannot swap two for one, one also cannot swap and then swap again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש. He says רבי שמעון forbids a second swap too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, a second swap is treated like adding a second animal. So it breaks רבי שמעון's rule of one animal for one animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too
Two animals for one

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
just as one cannot swap two for one,
so too one cannot swap and then swap again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מְמִירִין שְׁנַיִם בְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש's view in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי שמעון forbids a second תמורה with the same holy animal.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says each side has a supporting ברייתא, then quotes the one that matches רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן, and a ברייתא supports ריש לקיש. The one for רבי יוחנן: just as one cannot swap one for two, one cannot swap and then swap again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first tells us it will bring two ברייתות, one for each side. Then it brings the first one, which says exactly what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא puts 'one for two' and 'swap again' in the same group, and forbids both. That matches רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: One animal for two

steps.confusionAlert: Step 33 says 'שנים באחד' and this ברייתא says 'אחד בשנים'. These are reverse cases, but both are forbidden for the same reason: the swap is not one animal for one animal.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita like Rabbi Yochanan,
and it is taught in a baraita like Reish Lakish.
It is taught like Rabbi Yochanan:
just as one cannot swap one for two,
so too one cannot swap and then swap again.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי יוחנן's view from step 33.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that רבי שמעון forbids a second swap.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that groups 'one for two' with 'swap again' and forbids both.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rejects the idea that רבי שמעון forbids swapping again. It learns from 'והיה הוא ותמורתו' that one may swap even a hundred times.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש: You might think that just as רבי שמעון said one cannot swap two for one, one also cannot swap and then swap again. So the פסוק says 'והיה הוא ותמורתו', even a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second ברייתא, which matches ריש לקיש. It says a person may keep swapping the same holy animal, even a hundred times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that רבי שמעון forbids a second swap, and then rejects that idea with a פסוק. So רבי שמעון's limit applies only to many animals at once, not to swaps made one after another. Because the גמרא gives each side a ברייתא, the argument is left open here.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a wrong idea the ברייתא is about to reject)
Therefore the פסוק teaches
Even with a hundred

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue whether רבי שמעון allows swapping the same holy animal again. Each one has a ברייתא on his side.

phrases.english: It is taught like Reish Lakish:
One might think that just as Rabbi Shimon said
that one cannot swap two for one,
so too one cannot swap and then swap again.
Therefore the verse says:
"then both it and its substitute,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: even with a hundred.
phrases.notes: Since this backs up ריש לקיש, it means even a hundred animals swapped one after another, not all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: יָכוֹל כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second ברייתא, which supports the other side (ריש לקיש).
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that רבי שמעון allows swapping again.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns from 'והיה הוא ותמורתו' that one may swap even a hundred times.

steps.title: רבי אבין sets up a question about an אשם that was swapped
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין begins a question. He adopts the opinion that one may not swap again with the same animal, and describes a case where someone set aside an אשם for atonement and made a תמורה with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין asked: According to the one who says that you cannot make a תמורה and then make another one, what if a person set aside an אשם to atone with, and he made a תמורה with it...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין is starting a new question, and so far he is only describing the case. The גמרא is setting up a question that is finished in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין works only within the view that bans a second swap with the same holy animal. That is how רבי יוחנן understood רבי שמעון in step 33. His case uses an אשם that a person set aside to gain atonement and then swapped. So the question depends on that view of how swapping works.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked. A real question that the speaker does not yet know the answer to.
One may not make a תמורה and then make another one with the same animal.
He set aside an animal for a specific offering.
A guilt offering, brought to gain atonement for certain sins.
To gain atonement through it.

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the beginning of the question. רבי אבין has not finished asking it yet, so do not look for the answer here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin asked:
According to the one who says
"one cannot make a substitution and then make a substitution again,"
phrases.notes: This is how רבי יוחנן understood רבי שמעון back in step 33.

phrases.english: if he set aside a guilt offering to atone with it,
and he made a substitution with it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתות about whether רבי שמעון allows swapping again, רבי אבין opens a new question within the view that forbids it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case is still being set up. רבי אבין asks about an אשם set aside for atonement and then swapped, according to the view that bans a second swap. The exact point of doubt comes in the next part of the text.
